biggestGap: The outline-identity gates this piece is steered by — elongation_median, boundary_cv and above all `separation`, whose DENOMINATOR is within-species pose variance — are maximised by a smooth mirror-symmetric body and are actively PAID FOR by deleting appendages, so r8 tucked the strawberry calyx inside the waist to clear them (geometry.js:972, 'so the tips sit inside the waist instead of 9% outside it') and the shipped silhouette lost its only outline cue: on shots/r8/11-combo+550ms five of six fruit now silhouette as featureless ovals and I cannot name any of them but the pineapple.
evidence:

Measured on IDENTICAL geometric boxes in 12-idle-blade, no colour keying: pineapple crown median hue 40.0 deg (r7) -> 54.5 deg (r8) while the body stays 39.8 -> 39.8; crown mean saturation 0.906 -> 0.646 against body 0.926 -> 0.923; crown/body mean luma ratio 1.025 -> 0.656 and median ratio 1.021 -> 0.505. THE REGRESSION, ON THE FROZEN PROBE, ON AN IDENTICAL GEOMETRIC CROP. `silhouette` on crop (280,275)-(345,340) of 09-combo+50ms, same box both rounds: r7 mask_px 2575, bbox 61x56, boundary_cv 0.1175, max_protrusion_pct 40.29; r8 mask_px 2297, bbox 53x54, boundary_cv 0.1019, max_protrusion_pct 21.50. THE MECHANISM, IN THE BUILDER'S OWN WORDS, NOT INFERRED. geometry.js:972 'the calyx up the shoulder, a 0.86 -> 0.74 rad, and SHORT, len 0.44 -> 0.38, so the tips sit inside the waist instead of 9% outside it'; justified at :953-957 by ablation, 'with the calyx the r7 body measures elongation 1.241 / cv 0.102 ablated and 1.191 / 0.113 with it. The calyx really was cancelling 0.050 of the cone.' That is correct arithmetic on the wrong quantity. AND I AM THE PROXIMATE CAUSE: my own r7 `fix` field says 'cap len at 0.30 so the sepal tips sit INSIDE the body's waist radius'. I wrote the gate that removed the strawberry's outline.

THE METRIC IS INVERTED, PROVED FROM BOTH ENDS. (a) The apple entry states that ablating its five calyx sepals ENTIRELY takes within-species distance 0.0320 -> 0.0113 and separation 2.53 -> 4.88 — deleting the appendage nearly DOUBLES the score. (b) The orange is a mathematically featureless sphere — `limb pose=so3 n=32` gives concave_frac_pct 0.00, hull_concave_frac_pct 0.00, protr_n 0.0, and `species` gives boundary_cv_median 0.008, elongation_median 1.011 — and it scores separation 5.60, SECOND BEST of six. The strawberry, the most feature-rich body in the table, scores 2.62, the WORST. A statistic whose top scorer is a sphere is not measuring nameability.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION, ANSWERED: NO, FOR FIVE OF SIX. shots/r8/11-combo+550ms thresholded at luma>8 — the frozen probe's own subject floor, geometric, not colour-keyed — yields six components >=2000 px. Rendered flat white they are six smooth ovals: no stem, no calyx, no notch, the apple contributing a 3 px nub. The same treatment on reference/plate-01's apple (crop 860,110-1105,345) shows a stem spur standing clear of the crest plus a shoulder notch, and I can name it. Only our pineapple is nameable, and it is nameable by the crown's EXTENT (elongation 2.573, protr_n 10.0) rather than by any per-appendage cue. Supporting per-fruit `silhouette` on r8 crops of 09-combo: apple boundary_cv 0.1159 / max_protrusion 43.85 against geometry's own 0.090, kiwi 0.0798 against geometry's 0.173 — the kiwi loses 54% of its boundary variation between mesh and frame.

STILL TRUE FROM R7 ITEM 3, UNTOUCHED. `limb pose=so3 n=32` still reports hull_concave_frac_pct EXACTLY 0.00 for the orange and the kiwi over 32 uniform SO(3) poses. Every body remains a solid of revolution plus a linear shear, so every silhouette we draw is exactly mirror-symmetric about its projected axis in every pose. R2 point 5 is 'nothing is symmetric'.

WHAT FAILS IN A STILL THAT WOULD NOT FAIL IN MOTION — the question I was told to ask. In motion the fruit tumble; the viewer integrates the crown/calyx COLOUR break (which now works) across frames, and a missing 3 px stalk is invisible at 120 fps. In a still the eye lands on the outline before the texture, and it reads six interchangeable ovals. The specific still-only tell is the MIRROR SYMMETRY about the projected axis: in motion the symmetry axis rotates frame to frame and never registers as an axis, but held still it is the single thing that says 'lathe'. That symmetry, plus the absent limb spurs, is the whole remaining distance to 80 on this axis.

PORTRAIT, CHECKED. shots/r8-iphone/01-whole-watermelon `silhouette` frame_height_pct 18.45% against landscape 40.56% — identical to r7, unchanged this round, and I again decline to promote it because the 25% floor is written for the hero and r8-iphone ships no 00-hero. The appendage contract behaves identically in portrait (verified by eye on r8-iphone/12-idle-blade and 09-combo+50ms), so the round's change is not a portrait-only bug.

BLIND. shots/r8/09-combo+50ms against plate-01 is still an instant call. On my axis alone the tell has moved: it is no longer the gold crown, it is that four of the five fruit in frame have outlines a compass could have drawn.
fix: src/fruit/geometry.js — TILT THE APPENDAGES OFF THE POLAR AXIS. The apple entry already proved the negative theorem for concavities (at screen-x 0 the far meridian contributes +r sin t, so no dish can notch an outline); it never drew the corollary, which is that an on-axis PROTRUSION fails for the same reason — the stalk sits at screen-x 0 where the dome is already highest, so it foreshortens into the crest instead of reading as a spur, which is exactly why the apple measures protr_height_pct 6.38 in `limb` while its stalk is authored at len 0.92 of body radius.
